title: Edit a principle
prompt:
# Story: Edit a principle

- **Story**: XXX-edit-principle
- **Created**: 2026-11-02
- **Status**: Draft

## Story

As a team member, I want to open a principle and change its name or its description, so that our principles stay true and
keep helping us decide.

## Acceptance tests

Opening

- [ ] **Given** the Principles tab with principles, **When** the user presses a card (or uses Enter or Space on it), **Then**
  a dialog titled "Edit principle" opens, with the Name and the Description filled in with what was saved, the Name field in
  focus, Cancel, and Save.
- [ ] **Given** the dialog just opened, **Then** Save is disabled, because nothing changed.
- [ ] **Given** a principle with no description, **When** it is opened, **Then** the Description is empty and shows its
  placeholder "What the team holds to, and why."

Changing and saving

- [ ] **Given** the dialog, **When** the user changes the name or the description, **Then** Save is enabled. **When** the user
  puts the text back as it was, **Then** Save is disabled again.
- [ ] **Given** a change, **When** the user presses Save, **Then** the card shows the new name and description, in the same
  place in the list, the dialog closes, and nothing else in the list changes.
- [ ] **Given** a name and a description with spaces around them, **When** Save, **Then** both are saved without the spaces.
- [ ] **Given** the user clears the name (or leaves only spaces), **When** Save, **Then** "Give the principle a name." shows
  under the field, the field is marked invalid, and nothing is saved. Typing in the field clears the message.
- [ ] **Given** the user clears the description, **When** Save, **Then** it is saved. The card then shows "Click to describe
  this principle." in italics.
- [ ] **Given** the user renames a principle, **Then** it is still the same principle: its position, and the name of its file in
  the repository, do not change.
- [ ] **Given** two principles with the same name, **When** one is renamed to the name of the other, **Then** it is saved. Names
  do not have to be different.

Closing without saving

- [ ] **Given** the dialog, **When** the user presses Cancel, the Close (X) button or Escape, **Then** it closes and the principle
  is as it was.
- [ ] **Given** nothing changed, **When** the user clicks outside the dialog, **Then** it closes. **Given** there are unsaved
  changes, **Then** a click outside does nothing.
- [ ] **Given** the user opens the same principle again after closing without saving, **Then** the dialog shows the saved text, not
  the discarded changes.

After saving

- [ ] **Given** an edited principle with a description, **Then** the next story, enabler or diagram that is drafted gets the new text
  under "Principles of the team".
- [ ] **Given** GitHub is connected, **Then** the next sync uploads the changed file, `principles/<identity>.md`, as a pull request.

## Business rules and constraints

- A principle is a name (a few words) and a description of one to three sentences: what the team holds to, and why, written so that it
  helps to decide between two options.
- A principle keeps its identity for life. The identity comes from the name when the principle is added (the first six words, lower-case,
  joined by "-") and is not recalculated on a rename.
- "Changed" means any difference from the saved text. Saving trims the spaces, so a change of spaces alone can be saved and change nothing.
- While the dialog is open, syncing is blocked ("Save or close the principle first") and a download from the repository waits.

## Out of scope

- Adding a principle, removing one, and AI help with the text (each is its own story), reordering, and a history of changes to a principle.

## Tasks

- [ ] Open the dialog from a card with the saved name and description, and the title "Edit principle".
- [ ] Make Save depend on a difference from the saved text, and trim both fields on save.
- [ ] Add the check for an empty name, cleared when the user types.
- [ ] Save a change by identity, in place, without changing the identity or the order.
- [ ] Add the closing rules: Cancel, X, Escape, and click outside only when nothing changed.
- [ ] Tell the page that a principle is open, so that sync is blocked and downloads wait.

---

# Reference

Files in `bwyn-frontend/spikes/home-page/`: `PrinciplesPractices.tsx` (the card and `PrincipleModal`) and `usePrinciples.ts`
(`save(id, name, text)`).

A spike detail worth keeping in mind when the story is built: Escape closes the dialog even with unsaved text, while a click outside does not.

tasks.text: Add an `EditPrincipleDialog` React component (UI layer, ADR-0007) that receives the saved name and description, opens with the Name field in focus, and renders the title "Edit principle", both fields, Cancel, and Save.
Wire the card's click, Enter, and Space handlers in the Principles tab to open `EditPrincipleDialog` with the selected principle's data (UI layer, ADR-0007).
Implement dirty-state tracking in the dialog's ViewModel (interface-adapters layer, ADR-0007) so that Save is enabled only when the trimmed current values differ from the saved values.
Implement the empty-name validation in the ViewModel: block Save, show "Give the principle a name." beneath the field, mark the field invalid, and clear the message on any keystroke.
Implement the `save(id, name, description)` use-case call (use-cases layer, ADR-0007) that trims both fields and updates the principle in place by identity, preserving its position and identity.
Update the card rendering to show the new name and description after a successful save, and to show "Click to describe this principle." in italics when the description is empty.
Implement the closing rules in the ViewModel: Cancel and X close unconditionally; Escape closes unconditionally; a click outside closes only when nothing has changed.
Expose a "principle dialog open" flag from the ViewModel so that the sync and download mechanisms can observe it and block or wait accordingly.
Write Jest unit tests for the ViewModel covering dirty-state, validation, trim-on-save, identity preservation, and each closing rule (ADR-0005).
Write a Jest component test for `EditPrincipleDialog` covering initial focus, placeholder text, Save disabled state, and the invalid-name message (ADR-0005).
Add or extend an ArchUnitTS rule to verify that `react-router-dom` and dialog-state imports do not appear in the use-cases or entities layers (ADR-0016).
Run the full frontend build and test suite and confirm it completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build).
Implement the `save(id, name, description)` use-case call (use-cases layer, ADR-0007) that trims both fields and updates the principle in place by identity, preserving its position.
Add a `PUT /api/principles/{id}` endpoint in the inbound adapter (`bwyn-rest`) that accepts `{ name, description }` and returns the updated principle (ADR-0008, ADR-0017, AE-0005).

Add an `UpdatePrincipleCommand` and its handler in the application layer (`bwyn-application`) that trims both fields, validates the name is non-blank, and updates the principle by identity (ADR-0017, AE-0005).
Add or extend the `Principle` aggregate in the domain core (`bwyn-core`) with an `update(name, description)` method that enforces the non-blank name invariant (ADR-0017, AE-0005).
Add or extend the outbound adapter (`bwyn-infrastructure`) to persist the updated principle via Spring Data JPA (ADR-0011, AE-0005).
Write a Testcontainers integration test for the repository that verifies the updated name and description are persisted and the principle's identity and position are unchanged (ADR-0012).
Write a unit test for the `UpdatePrincipleCommand` handler covering trim-on-save, blank-name rejection, and identity preservation (ADR-0009).
Extend ArchUnit rules to verify that the `UpdatePrincipleCommand` handler in `*.application.*` has no dependency on `*.adapter.*` (ADR-0009, AE-0005).

Implement the `save(id, name, description)` use-case call (use-cases layer, ADR-0007) that calls the `PUT /api/principles/{id}` endpoint through an outbound port and updates the principle in place by identity, preserving its position.
